page.layout: Two engraved medallions at the top, side by side; below them one column of running text in two paragraphs; signature "Kk" at the foot, right.

main_text.l: M. VALERIVS adolescens Trib.militum, adversus Gal-
lum provocatorem solus, omnibus territis, processit: corvus
repente galeae eius insedit: dictu mirabile, quoties certamen initu
est, levans se alis, os, oculosque hostis, rostro & unguibus appe-
tiit: donec territum prodigij talis visu, oculisque simul ac mete
turbatum, Valerius obtruncat, anno mundi 3617. ante Chri-
stum, natum 345. Consul laudatum Valerium decem bobus,
aureaq; corona donat: inde Corvinus dictus, summo populi fa-
vore annos natus 23. Consul renuntiatur. Ti. Li. li. 7. c. 1. Dec. Eut,
li. 2. Oro. li. 3. ca. 6. Au. Gel. li. 9. ca. 11. Statuam Corvino Augustus
erexit, in cuius capite corvi effigies erat, pugnae monimentum.
Vixit Corvinus centum annos, interque primum & sextum con-
sulatum intercesserunt anni 46. Valer. li. 8. ca. 14.
M. CVRIVS Dentatus Consul Rom. Samnium diruit
funditus, anno mundi 3673. ante Christum natum 289. tunc
bellum 49. annis cum Samnitibus gestum, finitum est: neque
ullus hostis intra Italiā fuit, qui Ro. antea usque adeo fatigaverit.
Huic Samnites magnum auri pondus publice missum attule-
runt, qui in agresti scamno, assidens foco, ac ligneo catino coe-
nans, vultumque risu soluens, Superuacuæ, inquit, legationis mini-

l.i: stri, narrate Samnitibus, M. Curium malle locupletibus imperare, quam
ipsum fieri locupletem: & mementote me nec acie vinci, nec pecunia

main_text.l: corrumpi posse. Idem Curius Italia Pyrrhum regem exegit: atque
ex praeda regia, qua exercitum urbemque ditauerat, nil attigit.
Eutro. lib. 2. Valer. lib. 4. cap. 3. & Pli.lib.8.cap.6.de elephantis
primum Romae visis.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions (coins) above the text. Left: head of a helmeted man with a raven on the helmet; legend "M. VALERIVS" on the left and "CORVINVS" on the right. Right: bearded head; legend "M CVRIVS" on the right and "COS" on the left. Legends are part of the engravings and are not transcribed as text. Page is clean, with no margin notes. Faint show-through of the reverse page is visible below the second paragraph and was ignored.
